sources.name: The Seattle Times via The Spokesman-Review

caption:
Amazon is in talks to buy AI startup Decart at a valuation of around $7 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported.

Decart's software helps AI models run on different chips, including Amazon's own Trainium. Anthropic walked away from a deal for the startup last month.

Would you bet $7 billion on a 3-year-old AI company?

slides.headline: Amazon may spend *$7 billion* on a 3-year-old AI startup that Anthropic walked away from

slides.heading: Inside the *$7 billion* talks
paras: Amazon is in talks to acquire Decart at a valuation of around $7 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Amazon declined to comment. Decart, founded in 2023, has not disclosed its revenue. In May it was valued at about $4 billion.

slides.heading: Why Amazon wants *Decart*
paras: Decart sells software that helps AI models run faster on chips from Nvidia, Google and Amazon. It could make moving models onto Amazon's Trainium chips easier.
Amazon has said Decart ran real-time video four times faster on Trainium at half the cost of GPUs.

slides.heading: Anthropic *walked away*
paras: Bloomberg reported in August that Anthropic was in talks to buy Decart for about $6 billion. Anthropic walked away in September after due diligence.
Nvidia, which invested in Decart in May, also held acquisition talks earlier, according to CTech.

paras.t: The Journal says a deal could come together soon.

slides.hook: Big Tech is buying its way into faster AI chips. Follow to see if Amazon closes this deal.
